title: The Prize That Changed the Game
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空例。実在の人物・調査結果・宇宙探査の手順・教育効果を示すものではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: An imaginary school introduces an award recognizing students who make thoughtful contributions to the everyday life of their classmates, hoping to draw attention to activities that are rarely acknowledged in conventional academic competitions.
sentences.ja: 架空の学校は級友の日常生活への思いやりある貢献を認める賞を導入し、通常の学業競争ではめったに評価されない活動に注意を向けようとする。

sentences.en: The committee initially encourages students to submit descriptions of helpful actions they have observed, including small acts of assistance that might otherwise remain unnoticed.
sentences.ja: 委員会は当初、生徒が観察した有益な行動の記述を、気づかれないかもしれない小さな援助も含め提出するよう促す。

sentences.en: Several teachers welcome the initiative because it provides an opportunity to recognize contributions made by students whose achievements are not easily represented by examination scores.
sentences.ja: 試験点数で成果を表しにくい生徒の貢献を認める機会を提供するので複数教師が取り組みを歓迎する。

sentences.en: However, a teacher wonders whether the introduction of a competitive award could change the circumstances under which students choose to offer assistance.
sentences.ja: しかし競争的な賞の導入で生徒が援助を選ぶ事情が変化し得るか教師は疑問に思う。

sentences.en: The committee considers a hypothetical situation in which a student begins performing helpful actions in places where those actions are likely to be observed and reported by other people.
sentences.ja: 委員会は他者に観察・報告されやすい場所で生徒が有益な行動を始める仮想状況を考える。

sentences.en: The assistance might still provide a genuine benefit to its recipients, even if the possibility of receiving recognition formed part of the student's motivation.
sentences.ja: 認知を得る可能性が動機の一部であっても援助は受け手に本物の利益を提供し得る。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the teachers recognize that the number of reported actions may become a less informative measure of contributions if students who provide support in less visible circumstances are systematically overlooked.
sentences.ja: それでも見えにくい状況で支援する生徒が体系的に見落とされるなら報告件数は貢献を示す尺度として情報量が少なくなり得ると認識する。

sentences.en: They therefore distinguish the consequences of an action from the circumstances in which the action becomes available for public recognition.
sentences.ja: そこで行動の影響と行動が公に認知される事情を区別する。

sentences.en: Another concern involves the people receiving assistance, whose experiences might not always correspond to the descriptions submitted by observers.
sentences.ja: 別の懸念は援助を受ける人々であり、その体験は観察者の提出記述と常に一致するとは限らない。

sentences.en: Someone may appreciate a friend's support without wanting the difficulties that made the support necessary to become publicly known through an award ceremony.
sentences.ja: 友人の支援をありがたく思っても支援を必要にした困難が表彰式で公になることを望まない人もいるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The committee recognizes that a process designed to celebrate generosity should not automatically require recipients to disclose personal circumstances so that someone else can receive a reward.
sentences.ja: 寛大さをたたえる過程が他の誰かが報酬を得るために受け手の個人的事情の公開を自動的に要求すべきでないと認識する。

sentences.en: It consequently considers forms of recognition that do not depend on making sensitive information about particular recipients available to the wider school community.
sentences.ja: そこで特定受け手の機微情報を学校全体に公開することに依存しない認知形式を検討する。

sentences.en: The teachers also discuss whether recognizing a variety of contributions without ranking every participant might better reflect the original purpose of the initiative.
sentences.ja: 全参加者を順位づけせず多様な貢献を認める方が当初目的をより反映するかも議論する。

sentences.en: Such an arrangement would not prevent every student from thinking about recognition when deciding whether to help someone, nor would it establish the moral quality of each action independently of its circumstances.
sentences.ja: そうした仕組みも援助するか決める際の認知意識を全生徒からなくすことはなく、事情から独立して各行動の道徳的質を確定もしない。

sentences.en: It might nevertheless reduce the pressure to compare contributions that differ considerably in their form, visibility, and significance to the people involved.
sentences.ja: それでも形式、可視性、関係者への重要性がかなり異なる貢献の比較圧力を減らし得る。

sentences.en: The fictional committee does not claim that one award design has been demonstrated to improve kindness in real schools; instead, it examines how a system of recognition might alter the activities it is intended to encourage.
sentences.ja: 架空委員会は一表彰設計が実校で親切を改善すると実証されたとは主張せず、認知制度が促したい活動をどう変え得るか調べる。

sentences.en: An institution can influence behavior not only through the actions it explicitly requires but also through the achievements to which it assigns public value.
sentences.ja: 組織は明示的に要求する行動だけでなく公的価値を付す成果によっても行動に影響し得る。

sentences.en: A reward may draw attention to valuable contributions while creating incentives that deserve careful examination in relation to the purpose of the reward itself.
sentences.ja: 報酬は価値ある貢献に注意を向けつつ報酬目的に照らして注意深い検討に値する誘因を作り得る。

sentences.en: Responsible recognition consequently requires attention to the people who benefit from helpful actions as well as the people whose actions are being celebrated.
sentences.ja: 責任ある認知はたたえられる行動者だけでなく有益な行動から利益を得る人々への注意も必要とする。

sentences.en: The imaginary award becomes an opportunity to ask what a community wishes to encourage and whether its way of expressing appreciation supports that intention.
sentences.ja: 架空の賞は共同体が何を促したいか、感謝の表し方がその意図を支えるか問う機会になる。

new action intended to improve something
actually what it claims to be

options: To replace every examination with a competition.
To recognize thoughtful contributions not easily captured by academic scores.
To distinguish wealthy students from other students.
To reward only students with the highest academic marks.
questions.explanation_ja: 学業点数以外の貢献を認める。

questions.prompt: What concern does a teacher raise?
options: Awards can never recognize any achievement.
The students lack any opportunities to help.
Every action must receive an identical reward.
Competition may alter the circumstances motivating helpful behavior.

questions.prompt: Why is visible assistance not necessarily worthless?
options: Motivation alone determines every consequence.
All observed actions are always morally superior.
A recipient may benefit even when the helper seeks recognition.
An award eliminates every personal motive.
questions.explanation_ja: 動機と実際の利益を区別。

questions.prompt: What could make the report count less informative?
options: Less visible contributions being systematically overlooked.
Every contribution being equally reported.
The committee recording the context of an action.
Students helping in many different forms.
questions.explanation_ja: 見えにくい貢献の見落とし。

questions.prompt: Why might a recipient object to an award ceremony?
options: They necessarily oppose every helpful action.
They wish to receive academic scores instead.
They cannot benefit from any assistance.
They may not want personal difficulties publicly disclosed.
questions.explanation_ja: 個人的事情の公開を望まない。

questions.prompt: What kind of recognition does the committee consider?
options: Recognition based on a public list of every difficulty.
Recognition that does not require disclosure of sensitive recipient information.
Recognition exclusively for observers.
Recognition that ignores the recipients completely.

questions.prompt: Why might non-ranked recognition be preferable?
options: It could reduce pressure to compare contributions with different qualities and contexts.
It guarantees that no one will think about recognition.
It proves every contribution has equal moral value.
It makes kindness independent of circumstances.
questions.explanation_ja: 異質な貢献の比較圧力を減らす。

questions.prompt: What does the fictional case not establish?
options: Possible tensions created by recognition.
The importance of examining incentives.
A proven award method that improves kindness in real schools.
The usefulness of considering recipient experiences.
questions.explanation_ja: 実校での効果は未実証。

options: Rules preventing any action.
Things that encourage particular actions.
Descriptions of earlier outcomes.
Personal circumstances that must be hidden.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the argument?
options: Recognition systems should be evaluated by how their incentives and consequences relate to their original purpose.
Every helpful act should be ranked publicly.
Seeking recognition makes any assistance worthless.
All forms of reward should be eliminated.
questions.explanation_ja: 表彰目的と誘因・影響を吟味する。
